claims.statement: At the end of 2025, 48% of Polish customers had remote-read meters; 4,836 households and about 27,000 small or microbusiness customers used dynamic-price contracts.
Poland had 1,636,673 grid-connected renewable microinstallations at the end of 2025, 99.9% of them photovoltaic, creating a large installed base distinct from the still-small dynamic-tariff segment.
PSE exposes current system and market reports and points integrators to its current API, so a low-cost market-signal prototype is technically plausible.
Installer distribution will make customer acquisition affordable and the scheduler will create enough net savings to support recurring pricing.

contrary_evidence: S1 shows household dynamic-price adoption was still only about 0.03%, so broad demand is not established.
S1 also shows large differences in achieved prices across suppliers, which means an optimizer cannot promise savings merely from switching tariffs.
Equipment APIs are fragmented, and commercial reuse of every relevant price feed must be checked rather than assumed.

economics.acquisition_route: Use the founder's family renewable installer as a design partner and first source of consenting customers, then license the same audit workflow to other small installers in Poland and CEE. No camera-led audience is required.
economics.founder_time: Part-time validation hypothesis; delivery burden remains untested.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A maintained library of device adapters, tariff rules and consented forecast-versus-actual results could shorten each new deployment and strengthen savings estimates. This is an operating advantage only if device access and reuse rights persist; it is not assumed to be a durable moat.
fingerprint.customer: Polish microbusinesses and households that already have PV plus a controllable battery, heat pump or EV charger; renewable installers act as the acquisition and installation channel.
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Use the founder's family renewable installer as a design partner and first source of consenting customers, then license the same audit workflow to other small installers in Poland and CEE. No camera-led audience is required.
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Start with a software-only audit that combines interval consumption, PV output, equipment constraints and public market signals to simulate safer load schedules. Add opt-in control only for supported devices after shadow-mode validation. Sell direct through installers on a wholesale-plus-subscription model.
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The end customer pays for a read-only 30-day shadow audit; if measured data supports a credible benefit, the customer pays an annual software fee and the installer can earn an integration margin. Payment is tied to delivery of the audit or activation, not assumed regulatory budget.
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A customer is considering a dynamic-price contract, adding storage, or discovering that exported PV energy and poorly timed loads are producing disappointing economics.

founder_fit: Direct pilot access through the family renewable-energy company
Strong match for data science, forecasting and automation skills
Read-only MVP is part-time-testable and limits capital and safety downside
Installer channel minimizes repeated founder-led selling
risks: Evidence of a workflow, transition, or loss does not yet establish recurring willingness to pay.
The proposed distribution and compounding mechanisms remain hypotheses pending buyer evidence.

title: Installer-channel flexibility audit and scheduler for Polish prosumers
uncertainties: Which inverter, meter, battery and heat-pump APIs are reliably accessible to a third party
Net savings after battery degradation, comfort constraints, tariffs and software fees
Installer support burden and willingness to share customer relationships
Whether customers will grant interval-data and control permissions
Pricing, buyer authority, and acquisition economics remain unvalidated at discovery.

First validation test: Recruit 10 consenting customers from the family company's installed base, run a 30-day read-only shadow simulation on two supported device combinations, and ask for a signed paid continuation before building control. Pass only if at least three customers pay and measured, constraint-adjusted savings exceed the proposed annual fee by a clearly disclosed margin; otherwise keep it as an audit service or stop.
